reasons: X and Z both caught the real problem: the original men's Tree Runner is Final Few (I confirmed sizes 8-10 only, $70 final-sale colours, same table as X), so ads for it would waste cold clicks. Z solved it by pointing every ad at the Tree Runner NZ, which is in stock sizes 9-14 at $100 with a verified 8.9 oz weight, Featherbed insole and free shipping; X lays out the stock honestly and offers three options but still writes the ads for the sold-out shoe, with NZ swaps as footnotes. Z adds spec-aware production notes, a character-count table, a test question per concept and a competitor-ad rationale, while X has richer storyboards and a very clean claims table. Y leans on an unverified rating and review count, invents a soda comparison and a socks-optional line, and lands cold traffic on a nearly sold-out shoe. All five angles are distinct in X and Z; Y's materials and wash concepts overlap more with each other.

biggest_flaw.X: Ads are written for a shoe that is nearly sold out; the NZ fix is left as optional footnotes.
biggest_flaw.Y: Rating and review-count hero ad cannot be verified, and the sizes problem is underplayed.
biggest_flaw.Z: A few unverifiable claims (true to size, no side logo, ad count) and concept 2 sells a quote written about the original.

best_thing.X: Exact, verified stock and price table plus claim-by-claim sourcing and explicit do-not-claim rules.
best_thing.Y: Tidy, concise concepts with clear visual specs and brand fonts and colours.
best_thing.Z: Redirects the whole set to the in-stock Tree Runner NZ with verified facts, and ships production-ready specs and test hypotheses.
